title: The coconut palm
overallInstruction: You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1–13, which are based on Reading Passage 1 below.
overallInstructionZh: 你应该用大约20分钟完成第1–13题；这些题目均以阅读文章1为依据。
bodyParagraphs: For millennia, the coconut has been central to the lives of Polynesian and Asian peoples. In the western world, on the other hand, coconuts have always been exotic and unusual, sometimes rare. The Italian merchant traveller Marco Polo apparently saw coconuts in South Asia in the late 13th century, and among the mid-14th-century travel writings of Sir John Mandeville there is mention of ‘great Notes of Ynde’ (great Nuts of India). Today, images of palm-fringed tropical beaches are clichés in the west to sell holidays, chocolate bars, fizzy drinks and even romance.

Typically, we envisage coconuts as brown cannonballs that, when opened, provide sweet white flesh. But we see only part of the fruit and none of the plant from which they come. The coconut palm has a smooth, slender, grey trunk, up to 30 metres tall. This is an important source of timber for building houses, and is increasingly being used as a replacement for endangered hardwoods in the furniture construction industry. The trunk is surmounted by a rosette of leaves, each of which may be up to six metres long. The leaves have hard veins in their centres which, in many parts of the world, are used as brushes after the green part of the leaf has been stripped away. Immature coconut flowers are tightly clustered together among the leaves at the top of the trunk. The flower stems may be tapped for their sap to produce a drink, and the sap can also be reduced by boiling to produce a type of sugar used for cooking.

Coconut palms produce as many as seventy fruits per year, weighing more than a kilogram each. The wall of the fruit has three layers: a waterproof outer layer, a fibrous middle layer and a hard, inner layer. The thick fibrous middle layer produces coconut fibre, ‘coir’, which has numerous uses and is particularly important in manufacturing ropes. The woody innermost layer, the shell, with its three prominent ‘eyes’, surrounds the seed. An important product obtained from the shell is charcoal, which is widely used in various industries as well as in the home as a cooking fuel. When broken in half, the shells are also used as bowls in many parts of Asia.

Inside the shell are the nutrients (endosperm) needed by the developing seed. Initially, the endosperm is a sweetish liquid, coconut water, which is enjoyed as a drink, but also provides the hormones which encourage other plants to grow more rapidly and produce higher yields. As the fruit matures, the coconut water gradually solidifies to form the brilliant white, fat-rich, edible flesh or meat. Dried coconut flesh, ‘copra’, is made into coconut oil and coconut milk, which are widely used in cooking in different parts of the world, as well as in cosmetics. A derivative of coconut fat, glycerine, acquired strategic importance in a quite different sphere, as Alfred Nobel introduced the world to his nitroglycerine-based invention: dynamite.

Their biology would appear to make coconuts the great maritime voyagers and coastal colonizers of the plant world. The large, energy-rich fruits are able to float in water and tolerate salt, but cannot remain viable indefinitely; studies suggest after about 110 days at sea they are no longer able to germinate. Literally cast onto desert island shores, with little more than sand to grow in and exposed to the full glare of the tropical sun, coconut seeds are able to germinate and root. The air pocket in the seed, created as the endosperm solidifies, protects the embryo. In addition, the fibrous fruit wall that helped it to float during the voyage stores moisture that can be taken up by the roots of the coconut seedling as it starts to grow.

There have been centuries of academic debate over the origins of the coconut. There were no coconut palms in West Africa, the Caribbean or the east coast of the Americas before the voyages of the European explorers Vasco da Gama and Columbus in the late 15th and early 16th centuries. 16th century trade and human migration patterns reveal that Arab traders and European sailors are likely to have moved coconuts from South and Southeast Asia to Africa and then across the Atlantic to the east coast of America. But the origin of coconuts discovered along the west coast of America by 16th century sailors has been the subject of centuries of discussion. Two diametrically opposed origins have been proposed: that they came from Asia, or that they were native to America. Both suggestions have problems. In Asia, there is a large degree of coconut diversity and evidence of millennia of human use – but there are no relatives growing in the wild. In America, there are close coconut relatives, but no evidence that coconuts are indigenous. These problems have led to the intriguing suggestion that coconuts originated on coral islands in the Pacific and were dispersed from there.

sentences.text: For millennia, the coconut has been central to the lives of Polynesian and Asian peoples.
sentences.translation: 数千年来，椰子一直是波利尼西亚和亚洲各族群生活的核心。
sentences.structure: 主干是 the coconut has been central to...；For millennia 前置说明这一重要性持续了极长时间，to the lives... 指明影响对象。首句以跨越千年的尺度确立椰子的生活基础地位。

vocabulary.meaning: 波利尼西亚的；波利尼西亚人的

sentences.text: In the western world, on the other hand, coconuts have always been exotic and unusual, sometimes rare.
sentences.translation: 而在西方世界，椰子一直显得异域而不同寻常，有时甚至十分罕见。
sentences.structure: 主干是 coconuts have always been exotic and unusual；In the western world 限定地域，on the other hand 与首句形成对照，sometimes rare 再补充稀缺性。作者由“生活核心”转向“异域之物”。

sentences.text: The Italian merchant traveller Marco Polo apparently saw coconuts in South Asia in the late 13th century, and among the mid-14th-century travel writings of Sir John Mandeville there is mention of ‘great Notes of Ynde’ (great Nuts of India).
sentences.translation: 据说，意大利商人兼旅行家马可·波罗在13世纪晚期于南亚见过椰子；而在14世纪中叶约翰·曼德维尔爵士的游记中，也提到了“印度的大坚果”。
sentences.structure: and 连接两条早期欧洲记录：前半主干是 Marco Polo apparently saw...，apparently 表示“据说/看来”，与事实保持证据距离而非断言确定；后半采用 there is mention of...，among... 前置定位文献。两个时间点说明椰子进入西方书写的过程。

vocabulary.meaning: 据说；看来（保留不确定性）

sentences.text: Today, images of palm-fringed tropical beaches are clichés in the west to sell holidays, chocolate bars, fizzy drinks and even romance.
sentences.translation: 如今，在西方，棕榈环绕的热带海滩图像已成了推销度假产品、巧克力棒、汽水，甚至浪漫情调的陈词滥调。
sentences.structure: 主干是 images ... are clichés；of palm-fringed tropical beaches 修饰 images，to sell... 表用途，and even romance 以递进收尾。作者指出椰子意象已被商业化。

sentences.text: Typically, we envisage coconuts as brown cannonballs that, when opened, provide sweet white flesh.
sentences.translation: 通常，我们会把椰子想象成棕色炮弹；打开后，它们会露出甜甜的白色果肉。
sentences.structure: 主干是 we envisage coconuts as...；that 引导定语从句修饰 cannonballs，when opened 是省略主语与 be 的时间状语。句子先呈现大众熟悉却片面的外观。

sentences.text: But we see only part of the fruit and none of the plant from which they come.
sentences.translation: 但我们看到的只是果实的一部分，对结出它们的植株却一无所见。
sentences.structure: 主干是 we see only part... and none...；两个宾语形成强烈对比，from which they come 修饰 plant。But 推翻上一句的完整性假象，引出全株结构。

vocabulary.meaning: 来自；本句指由植株结出

sentences.text: The coconut palm has a smooth, slender, grey trunk, up to 30 metres tall.
sentences.translation: 椰子树有一根光滑、细长的灰色树干，高度可达30米。
sentences.structure: 主干是 The coconut palm has...；smooth, slender, grey 三个形容词并列修饰 trunk，up to 30 metres tall 补充高度。句子从整体外形进入部位说明。

sentences.text: This is an important source of timber for building houses, and is increasingly being used as a replacement for endangered hardwoods in the furniture construction industry.
sentences.translation: 树干是建房木材的重要来源，而且在家具制造业中，正日益被用来替代濒危的硬木。
sentences.structure: 两个并列谓语是 is an important source... 与 is increasingly being used...；This 回指 trunk，for building houses 表用途，as a replacement for... 表替代关系。句子同时说明传统用途与环保价值。

sentences.text: The trunk is surmounted by a rosette of leaves, each of which may be up to six metres long.
sentences.translation: 树干顶端是一簇呈莲座状排列的叶片，每片叶子最长可达六米。
sentences.structure: 主干是 The trunk is surmounted by...；each of which 引导非限制性定语从句，逐一补充叶片长度。被动结构把视线从树干向上移到树冠。

sentences.text: The leaves have hard veins in their centres which, in many parts of the world, are used as brushes after the green part of the leaf has been stripped away.
sentences.translation: 叶片中央有坚硬的叶脉；在世界许多地方，剥去叶子的绿色部分后，这些叶脉会被当作刷子使用。
sentences.structure: 主干是 The leaves have hard veins；which 从句修饰 veins，in many parts... 插入说明地域，after 从句说明制作刷子前的处理步骤。

vocabulary.term: in many parts of the world

sentences.text: Immature coconut flowers are tightly clustered together among the leaves at the top of the trunk.
sentences.translation: 尚未成熟的椰子花紧密地簇生在树干顶部的叶片之间。
sentences.structure: 主干是 Immature coconut flowers are tightly clustered；among... 与 at the top... 逐层定位。被动结构突出花朵紧密成簇的状态。

sentences.text: The flower stems may be tapped for their sap to produce a drink, and the sap can also be reduced by boiling to produce a type of sugar used for cooking.
sentences.translation: 花梗可以被割开取汁来制作饮料；树液也可以通过熬煮浓缩，制成一种烹饪用糖。
sentences.structure: and 连接两种树液用途；may be tapped... 与 can be reduced... 都是被动结构，两个 to produce 表目的，used for cooking 后置修饰 sugar。

sentences.text: Coconut palms produce as many as seventy fruits per year, weighing more than a kilogram each.
sentences.translation: 椰子树每年最多可结70个果实，每个重量超过一千克。
sentences.structure: 主干是 Coconut palms produce...；as many as 强调数量之多，weighing... 是现在分词短语，补充每个果实的重量。

sentences.text: The wall of the fruit has three layers: a waterproof outer layer, a fibrous middle layer and a hard, inner layer.
sentences.translation: 果壁有三层：防水的外层、纤维质的中层和坚硬的内层。
sentences.structure: 主干是 The wall of the fruit has three layers；冒号后列出三层结构，outer、middle、inner 按由外向内的顺序组织信息。

sentences.text: The thick fibrous middle layer produces coconut fibre, ‘coir’, which has numerous uses and is particularly important in manufacturing ropes.
sentences.translation: 厚厚的纤维质中层可产出椰纤维，即“椰壳纤维”；它用途众多，在制绳业中尤其重要。
sentences.structure: 主干是 The ... layer produces coconut fibre；coir 是同位语，which 从句修饰 coir，内部 has 与 is 并列。句子把结构、材料名称和核心用途连在一起。

sentences.text: The woody innermost layer, the shell, with its three prominent ‘eyes’, surrounds the seed.
sentences.translation: 最里面的木质层就是椰壳；它带有三个醒目的“眼”，包围着种子。
sentences.structure: 主干是 The woody innermost layer surrounds the seed；the shell 是同位语，with... 是附加说明。三个“眼”的视觉细节帮助识别椰壳。

sentences.text: An important product obtained from the shell is charcoal, which is widely used in various industries as well as in the home as a cooking fuel.
sentences.translation: 从椰壳中获得的一种重要产品是木炭；木炭广泛用于各种工业，也在家庭中用作烹饪燃料。
sentences.structure: 主干是 An important product is charcoal；obtained from... 修饰 product，which 从句补充木炭用途，as well as 连接工业与家庭两类场景。

sentences.text: When broken in half, the shells are also used as bowls in many parts of Asia.
sentences.translation: 椰壳劈成两半后，在亚洲许多地区还会被用作碗。
sentences.structure: When broken in half 是省略主语与 be 的时间状语；主干是 the shells are also used as bowls，in many parts of Asia 说明地域。

sentences.text: Inside the shell are the nutrients (endosperm) needed by the developing seed.
sentences.translation: 椰壳内部是发育中的种子所需的营养物质，即胚乳。
sentences.structure: 这是地点状语前置引起的完全倒装，正常语序为 The nutrients ... are inside the shell；endosperm 是 nutrients 的专业同位说明，needed by... 后置修饰。

sentences.text: Initially, the endosperm is a sweetish liquid, coconut water, which is enjoyed as a drink, but also provides the hormones which encourage other plants to grow more rapidly and produce higher yields.
sentences.translation: 起初，胚乳是一种略带甜味的液体，也就是椰子水；它既可作为饮料享用，也能提供促使其他植物生长更快、产量更高的激素。
sentences.structure: 主干是 the endosperm is a ... liquid；coconut water 是同位语，which 从句中 is enjoyed 与 provides 由 but also 连接，第二个 which 修饰 hormones，grow 与 produce 并列。

sentences.text: As the fruit matures, the coconut water gradually solidifies to form the brilliant white, fat-rich, edible flesh or meat.
sentences.translation: 随着果实成熟，椰子水逐渐凝固，形成亮白色、富含脂肪且可食用的果肉。
sentences.structure: As 从句表示随时间发生的变化；主干是 the coconut water gradually solidifies，to form... 表结果。三个形容词依次描写颜色、营养与可食用性。

sentences.text: Dried coconut flesh, ‘copra’, is made into coconut oil and coconut milk, which are widely used in cooking in different parts of the world, as well as in cosmetics.
sentences.translation: 干燥的椰肉称为“椰干”，可制成椰子油和椰奶；二者在世界不同地区广泛用于烹饪，也用于化妆品。
sentences.structure: 主干是 Dried coconut flesh is made into...；copra 是同位语，which 从句共同修饰 coconut oil and coconut milk，as well as 追加化妆品用途。

vocabulary.term: in different parts of the world

sentences.text: A derivative of coconut fat, glycerine, acquired strategic importance in a quite different sphere, as Alfred Nobel introduced the world to his nitroglycerine-based invention: dynamite.
sentences.translation: 椰子脂肪的一种衍生物——甘油——在一个截然不同的领域获得了战略重要性，因为阿尔弗雷德·诺贝尔向世界推出了他以硝化甘油为基础的发明——炸药。
sentences.structure: 主干是 A derivative ... acquired strategic importance；glycerine 是同位语，as 从句说明其战略意义产生的背景；nitroglycerine-based 明确表示该发明以硝化甘油为基础，冒号后的 dynamite 与 invention 构成同位解释。该跨页句把日常椰制品突然连接到工业炸药。

vocabulary.meaning: 向全世界推出；使世界认识

sentences.text: Their biology would appear to make coconuts the great maritime voyagers and coastal colonizers of the plant world.
sentences.translation: 椰子的生物特性似乎使它们成为植物界杰出的海上航行者和海岸殖民者。
sentences.structure: 主干是 Their biology would appear to make coconuts...；make 后接宾语与宾补，would appear to 谨慎表达推断。拟人化的 voyagers 与 colonizers 引出海洋传播机制。

vocabulary.meaning: 拓殖者；扩散并定居的物种

sentences.text: The large, energy-rich fruits are able to float in water and tolerate salt, but cannot remain viable indefinitely; studies suggest after about 110 days at sea they are no longer able to germinate.
sentences.translation: 这种硕大、富含能量的果实能够漂浮在水上并耐受盐分，却无法无限期保持活性；研究表明，在海上约110天后，它们便不能再发芽。
sentences.structure: 分号前由 but 对比 are able to... 与 cannot remain...；分号后主干是 studies suggest，省略 that 的宾语从句给出约110天的生存界限。

sentences.text: Literally cast onto desert island shores, with little more than sand to grow in and exposed to the full glare of the tropical sun, coconut seeds are able to germinate and root.
sentences.translation: 椰子种子即使真的被抛上海岛荒岸，几乎只有沙土可供生长，又暴露在热带烈日的强光下，仍能发芽并扎根。
sentences.structure: 主干是 coconut seeds are able to germinate and root；句首过去分词 cast... 与 exposed... 描写被动处境，with... 补充贫瘠条件。重重逆境置于主句前，突出种子生命力。

sentences.text: The air pocket in the seed, created as the endosperm solidifies, protects the embryo.
sentences.translation: 种子里的气腔在胚乳凝固时形成，能够保护胚。
sentences.structure: 主干是 The air pocket ... protects the embryo；in the seed 修饰 air pocket，created... 是过去分词短语，as 从句说明形成时机。

sentences.text: In addition, the fibrous fruit wall that helped it to float during the voyage stores moisture that can be taken up by the roots of the coconut seedling as it starts to grow.
sentences.translation: 此外，曾帮助果实在航程中漂浮的纤维质果壁还能储存水分；椰子幼苗开始生长时，根部可以吸收这些水分。
sentences.structure: 主干是 the fibrous fruit wall stores moisture；第一个 that 从句修饰 fruit wall，第二个 that 从句修饰 moisture，as 从句说明吸水发生的生长阶段。

sentences.text: There have been centuries of academic debate over the origins of the coconut.
sentences.translation: 关于椰子起源的学术争论已经持续了数百年。
sentences.structure: There have been... 是存在句，centuries of 强调时间跨度，over the origins... 指明争论主题。句子由传播能力转入起源之谜。

sentences.text: There were no coconut palms in West Africa, the Caribbean or the east coast of the Americas before the voyages of the European explorers Vasco da Gama and Columbus in the late 15th and early 16th centuries.
sentences.translation: 在15世纪末至16世纪初欧洲探险家瓦斯科·达·伽马和哥伦布航行之前，西非、加勒比地区和美洲东海岸都没有椰子树。
sentences.structure: There were no... 是存在句；三个地点并列，before... 建立历史时间界线，of the European explorers... 说明航行者。该事实限定了人类传播的时间。

sentences.text: 16th century trade and human migration patterns reveal that Arab traders and European sailors are likely to have moved coconuts from South and Southeast Asia to Africa and then across the Atlantic to the east coast of America.
sentences.translation: 16世纪的贸易与人口迁移模式表明，阿拉伯商人和欧洲水手很可能把椰子从南亚和东南亚带到非洲，随后又越过大西洋带到美洲东海岸。
sentences.structure: 主干是 trade and human migration patterns reveal that...；that 从句中 are likely to have moved 表对过去行为的高度可能推断，from...to...and then across... 勾勒传播路线。

sentences.text: But the origin of coconuts discovered along the west coast of America by 16th century sailors has been the subject of centuries of discussion.
sentences.translation: 但16世纪水手在美洲西海岸发现的椰子究竟源自何处，数百年来一直是人们讨论的主题。
sentences.structure: 主干是 the origin ... has been the subject...；discovered... 是过去分词短语修饰 coconuts，by... 指明发现者，But 表明西海岸样本无法由上一句路线直接解释。

sentences.text: Two diametrically opposed origins have been proposed: that they came from Asia, or that they were native to America.
sentences.translation: 人们提出了两种截然相反的起源说：椰子来自亚洲，或椰子原产于美洲。
sentences.structure: 主干是 Two ... origins have been proposed；冒号后两个 that 从句作同位解释，由 or 连接。被动语态把焦点放在两种假说而非提出者身上。

vocabulary.meaning: 截然相反的；完全对立的

sentences.text: Both suggestions have problems.
sentences.translation: 两种说法都存在问题。
sentences.structure: 主干是 Both suggestions have problems；Both 承接上一句的两个 that 从句。短句像一个转轴，开启对两方证据缺口的逐一说明。

sentences.text: In Asia, there is a large degree of coconut diversity and evidence of millennia of human use – but there are no relatives growing in the wild.
sentences.translation: 在亚洲，椰子具有很高的多样性，也有证据显示人类已使用椰子数千年——但野外没有它的近缘种。
sentences.structure: 破折号前后是两个 there be 结构；前半列出支持亚洲起源的 diversity 与 evidence，but 后给出反证缺口。对照结构呈现一项假说的强证据与难题。

sentences.text: In America, there are close coconut relatives, but no evidence that coconuts are indigenous.
sentences.translation: 在美洲，存在椰子的近缘种，却没有证据表明椰子是当地原生的。
sentences.structure: 主干是 there are close coconut relatives, but no evidence；后半省略 there is，that 从句说明 evidence 的具体内容。它与上一句形成镜像：有近缘种，却缺人类原生证据。

sentences.text: These problems have led to the intriguing suggestion that coconuts originated on coral islands in the Pacific and were dispersed from there.
sentences.translation: 这些问题催生了一个耐人寻味的观点：椰子起源于太平洋的珊瑚岛，之后再从那里传播开来。
sentences.structure: 主干是 These problems have led to the ... suggestion；that 从句解释 suggestion，其中 originated 与 were dispersed 并列，分别说明起点和扩散。结尾提出第三种调和性假说。

vocabulary.meaning: 耐人寻味的；引人入胜的

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 9–13 on your answer sheet, write
TRUE if the statement agrees with the information
FALSE if the statement contradicts the information
NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this
questionSections.instructionZh: 下列陈述是否与阅读文章1中的信息一致？在答题纸第9–13题的方框内填写：TRUE（陈述与文章信息一致）；FALSE（陈述与文章信息矛盾）；NOT GIVEN（文章没有相关信息）。

options.label: TRUE
options.translation: 正确：陈述与文章信息一致

options.label: FALSE
options.translation: 错误：陈述与文章信息矛盾

options.label: NOT GIVEN
options.translation: 未提及：文章没有足够信息判断

questions.prompt: timber for houses and the making of 1 __________
questions.evidence: is increasingly being used as a replacement for endangered hardwoods in the furniture construction industry
questions.explanation: making of 对应 construction industry；树干木材用于家具制造，答案取原文 furniture。
questions.distractorAnalysis: houses 已直接给出；hardwoods 是被替代的材料，不是成品。

questions.prompt: stems provide sap, used as a drink or a source of 2 __________
questions.promptZh: 花梗提供树液，可作饮料或作为__________的来源
questions.evidence: the sap can also be reduced by boiling to produce a type of sugar used for cooking
questions.explanation: source of 对应 produce a type of；树液熬煮后制成 sugar。
questions.distractorAnalysis: sap 是来源物，drink 是另一用途，cooking 是糖的用途。

questions.evidence: coir, which has numerous uses and is particularly important in manufacturing ropes
questions.explanation: used for 对应 important in manufacturing；原文复数 ropes 可直接填入。
questions.distractorAnalysis: coir/fibre 是材料本身，manufacturing 是过程，不是制成品。

questions.evidence: An important product obtained from the shell is charcoal
questions.explanation: a source of 改写 obtained from the shell；产物是 charcoal。
questions.distractorAnalysis: fuel 是木炭的用途；shell 是来源部位。

questions.evidence: When broken in half, the shells are also used as bowls
questions.explanation: halved 对应 broken in half，used as 后的 bowls 即答案。
questions.distractorAnalysis: shells 是原材料；half 描述处理方式。

questions.prompt: a source of 6 __________ for other plants
questions.promptZh: 是供其他植物使用的__________的来源
questions.evidence: provides the hormones which encourage other plants to grow more rapidly and produce higher yields
questions.explanation: a source of 对应 provides；作用对象 other plants 在原文直接出现。
questions.distractorAnalysis: nutrients 位于胚乳中但服务于 developing seed；yields 是结果。

questions.prompt: oil and milk for cooking and 7 __________
questions.evidence: coconut oil and coconut milk, which are widely used in cooking ... as well as in cosmetics
questions.explanation: and 对应 as well as；与 cooking 并列的用途是 cosmetics。
questions.distractorAnalysis: copra 是原料，oil/milk 已在题干中。

questions.evidence: A derivative of coconut fat, glycerine ... his nitroglycerine-based invention: dynamite
questions.explanation: 题干 ingredient in 概括甘油与硝化甘油发明的关系；冒号明确 invention 是 dynamite。
questions.distractorAnalysis: nitroglycerine-based 超过一个词且是修饰语；invention 是上位词。

questions.prompt: Coconut seeds need shade in order to germinate.
questions.promptZh: 椰子种子需要阴凉处才能发芽。
questions.evidence: exposed to the full glare of the tropical sun, coconut seeds are able to germinate and root
questions.explanation: 题干说需要 shade，原文却说暴露在热带烈日强光下仍能发芽，信息直接矛盾。
questions.distractorAnalysis: TRUE 颠倒生长条件；NOT GIVEN 忽略了 full glare 与 germinate 的直接联系。

questions.prompt: Coconuts were probably transported to Asia from America in the 16th century.
questions.promptZh: 16世纪，椰子可能从美洲被运往亚洲。
questions.evidence: are likely to have moved coconuts from South and Southeast Asia to Africa and then across the Atlantic to the east coast of America
questions.explanation: 原文路线从亚洲出发，经非洲到美洲；题干把方向完全倒置。
questions.distractorAnalysis: TRUE 属方向倒置；NOT GIVEN 不成立，因为路线明确给出。

questions.prompt: Coconuts found on the west coast of America were a different type from those found on the east coast.
questions.promptZh: 在美洲西海岸发现的椰子与东海岸发现的是不同类型。
questions.evidence: the origin of coconuts discovered along the west coast of America ... has been the subject of centuries of discussion
questions.explanation: 原文分别讨论东西海岸椰子的到达与起源，但没有比较两者是否属于不同类型。
questions.distractorAnalysis: TRUE/ FALSE 都需要类型比较证据，原文只谈 origin。

questions.prompt: All the coconuts found in Asia are cultivated varieties.
questions.promptZh: 亚洲发现的所有椰子都是栽培品种。
questions.evidence: In Asia, there is a large degree of coconut diversity and evidence of millennia of human use – but there are no relatives growing in the wild.
questions.explanation: 原文明说亚洲野外没有椰子的近缘野生种，并以长期人类利用和多样性描述亚洲椰子；这支持亚洲所见椰子均为栽培类型。
questions.distractorAnalysis: FALSE 会把 diversity 误读成存在野生品种；NOT GIVEN 忽略 no relatives growing in the wild。

questions.prompt: Coconuts are cultivated in different ways in America and the Pacific.
questions.promptZh: 美洲和太平洋地区采用不同方式种植椰子。
questions.evidence: These problems have led to the intriguing suggestion that coconuts originated on coral islands in the Pacific and were dispersed from there.
questions.explanation: 原文讨论美洲的近缘种、原生证据和太平洋起源假说，没有比较两地的种植方式。
questions.distractorAnalysis: TRUE/ FALSE 都需要 cultivation methods 的对比，文中没有。
